record_notes.DCP-LETT-1399: April 17, 1851 is inferred from arrival at Malvern and Emma Thursday-evening endorsement. Four oclock in the header follows a footnote marker, not a numeral 24. Annie recognizes Darwin; he reports guarded hope, no suffering and a proposed later update if he meets Gully, while urging pregnant Emma not to travel. P3 reiterates reported improvement. The editorial quotation of Fanny Allen April 18 letter is a separate voice and witness, not the incoming prompt. No matched surviving Emma input.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1400: April 18 report has nonchronological display order: P2 at noon, P3 at one and three oclock, then P1 at four oclock in the space left at the head for the final account. Footnote 1 explicitly confirms this; twelve is noon, not midnight. Gully stayed the preceding night. Pulse, vomiting, gruel and brandy reports preserve uncertainty rather than a steady recovery. Your note made me cry refers to unlocated Emma text, not later April 19 notes. Maer illness is an analogy, not a diagnosis. Preserve physical order separately from time order.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1401: Second April 18 Friday report starts at seven with Gully absent and adds his assessment at 7:30 PM. Darwin perceived danger, but Gully still sees hope without worsening key symptoms. A fourth vomiting episode appears in the final paragraph. One separate outgoing update, not merged with 1400; no specific surviving incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1402: April 19 Saturday starts at eleven after a nine AM electric telegram. P3 adds two, three, four and five PM updates. MathML gives the earlier doctor visit as eight and a half, not 812. P2 acknowledges an unidentified Emma note, not the later same-day Down 4:15 note. Etty travels to London that day and Leith Hill Monday; Fanny has arrived and Hensleigh passes through. Excluded authorial text proposes two letters for safety, but 1406 says no second later letter was sent. Keep intention separate from dispatch. Expected telegram arrival is not itself receipt proof.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1404: April 19 Emma letter specifically echoes 1400 report of Gully sleeping in the house and asks Darwin to let Fanny watch so he is not exhausted. The precious look may recall 1399, but only the doctor sleep detail uniquely binds the accepted reverse edge here. Aunt F is Fanny Allen at Down, distinct from Fanny Mackintosh Wedgwood at Malvern. Sunday postal uncertainty and proposed Monday Etty return remain expectations. This precedes the separate 4:15 message acknowledgement 1405.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1405: April 19 Saturday quarter past four, verified from header MathML: 16:15. A hopeful message has just arrived with John Griffiths while Emma seeks a flower in Annie garden. Telegram 1403, forwarded through Erasmus to Down by fly, and 1402 dispatch witness identify this message. It is not receipt of the postal 1402 letter still being composed later that afternoon. Messenger employment remains editorially probable. Preserve the abbreviated salutation without replacing it with a later editorial expansion. The garden passage is explicitly answered in 1408 P3.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1406: April 20 Sunday covers the prior night and morning before eight, then updates at eight, ten, noon, two, three and 4:30 PM. Two Emma notes arrive within P3 at eight. The following assurance that Darwin does not sit constantly with Annie answers 1404 watching and exhaustion concern. 1405 may be the other note, but a count alone does not prove identity; its garden passage is explicitly answered next day. Exclude P1–2 and the first doctor report within P3 from the response to newly arrived notes. Doctor and surgeon opinions remain attributed and uncertain. No second later Saturday letter was sent.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1408: April 21 Monday begins with a retrospective and an eight AM assessment, followed by noon and three PM updates. Vinegar washing, bladder and bowel function, fever and hope fluctuate. P2 concerns sisters Susan and Catherine and a possible Wednesday visit. P3 explicitly answers the garden and flower passage in 1405; its earlier receipt day is not proved. Use that narrowly identified reply section rather than unrelated daily updates. Fanny caregiving during the night of April 20–21 is distinct from her Saturday April 19 note identified in 1409 apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1408A: Separate April 21 Monday 7:30 PM update: enjoyed tea, question about Etty, reassuring doctor, renewed need for the surgeon, tranquil sleep and vinegar washing. It follows the three PM ending of 1408 and cannot have reached Emma before her Monday noon letter 1409. It is one of the explicitly Monday pair answered Tuesday in 1410. No uniquely identified incoming prompt for this evening update.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1409: April 21 Monday noon: two Darwin letters and Fanny note have arrived. Hourly-account wording and Etty London/Leith Hill uncertainty fit Saturday 1402 and Sunday 1406; 1406 says no second later Saturday letter was sent. The Monday reports completed at three PM and 7:30 PM are impossible antecedents. Emma has lived on Saturday telegram words until now, sends a thirty-second sandglass, anticipates Elizabeth on Wednesday and discusses pregnancy. Later birth and Tuesday arrival dates are editorial facts, not changes to her current expectations. Darwin receipt is unproved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1410: P1–3 were composed Tuesday April 22, then the note returned because Malvern was omitted from the address. P4–5 were added Wednesday April 23. Tuesday explicitly answers the two Monday letters 1408 and 1408A; bowel action and Catherine concern specifically match 1408. Optimism precedes later deterioration news. Tuesday composition does not establish Tuesday availability to Darwin, and later receipt is unproved. Chloroform preparation concerns Emma impending confinement, not Annie treatment.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1411: Wednesday April 23 before-post P1–3 reread Monday 1408, explicitly recall vinegar sponging, offer foods tentatively, discuss family support, quote Caroline and report Willy and Franky. After-post P4 abruptly shifts to distress after Fanny April 22 deterioration letter, reproduced in footnote 7; it is not acknowledgement of Darwin same-day death notice 1412. Preserve the original Tuesday 21st dating variant and editorial correction to April 22. Fanny reports Darwin withheld an optimistic Tuesday letter; do not invent a sent source. Final pencil text ends unfinished after dear F. Historical family and medical reports remain attributed source material.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1412: Wednesday April 23 announces Annie death at noon, peaceful passing, a short happy life, gratitude for the photograph, and mutual support for Emma. Darwin is unwell and return timing remains uncertain. Hope that Fanny note prepared Emma does not establish receipt of Emma 1410 or 1411 that day. No supported incoming prompt. Daguerreotype date and later frontispiece details are editorial apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1414: Thursday April 24 before noon starts with mourning inferred from the absence of a promised improvement message and asks about the withheld optimistic letter known through Fanny. Mid-P1, Your letter is just come marks arrival of Darwin 1412 death notice. Only following text can answer that notice; the happy innocent life wording supplies a distinctive match. Earlier grief does not prove prior reading of 1412. Return hopes also draw on Fanny Wednesday six PM letter; 1412 does not promise an exact departure. P3 adds Willy reaction. No Darwin reading of this Emma response is established.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1403: Additional complete April 19 telegram to catalogued recipient Erasmus Alvey Darwin asks for a man via Sydenham station and fly to Down with Annie rally, good night and less imminent danger news. Saturday nine AM matches 1402 dispatch witness. The form literally reads F. Darwin at 7 Park Street; preserve that variant without inventing another identity. Emma 1405 responds to the delivered message, not the postal 1402 letter. No synthetic relay wording or messenger account is created.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1178: Explicit prior primary context reading reused with matching pins. Tuesday assigned May23,1848. Children Willy/Annie notes and Emma letter separately thanked. Short Roman-cream passage read aloud quoted as Darwin reports it, not full incoming text. Father health mixed; private preference for rural home current. Erasmus note this morning with Fanny/party gossip is another missing input; attraction is Darwin inference, not direct stated fact. Children invitation deliberately left open, presents obtained. Current Sévigné appreciation not proof completed entire edition. No text to reconstruct family prompts.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1179: Explicit prior primary context reading reused with matching pins. Thursday assigned May25,1848. Father health and Catherine departure reported; Owens are William Mostyn Owen family, not Richard Owen. Third note to chemist Blunt just written, contents missing. Erasmus joke about Lyells, Queen ball and Prince speech attributed and not evidence Darwin attended. Annie singing response follows missing Emma letter. Historical racialized self-description in closing is actual source language; later editorial endearment interpretation must remain apparatus, not replace or expand other abbreviations. Sévigné enthusiasm continues. No incoming family source identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1180: Explicit prior primary context reading reused with matching pins. Saturday–Sunday May27–28,1848. P1 Saturday acknowledges morning Emma baby-health letter and reports own attack, deaths/family news, uncertain Monday travel. P2–4 Sunday acknowledges a further nice note, reports sleepless night and now abandons tomorrow departure. New Sunday information must not condition Saturday prose. Henrietta little letter thanked in final postscript, precise earlier receipt unknown. Baby identity Elizabeth distinct from adult Elizabeth supporting Emma. Later June1 return not completed at either dateline. No missing Emma or child text reconstructed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1208: Explicit prior primary context reading reused with matching pins. Three oclock at Park Street, assigned November17,1848. Arrival, rest and affection to Emma; no explicit incoming letter prompt. Emma verso note establishes November1848 Shrewsbury journey, narrower day supplied editorially in funeral itinerary. Letter does not state all funeral details or Erasmus whereabouts; keep apparatus apart. Health and emotional support are Darwin own voice, eligible grounding in principle without synthetic question.

reading_method: Fourteen targets and additional telegram 1403 independently read in full, including excluded authorial text, original date constraints, footnotes and bibliography. MathML in 1402 and 1405 inspected. Four 1848 contexts reuse explicit accepted primary readings with matching note, ledger and source hashes. Arrival boundaries and chronology adjudicated independently.
